original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: Exact unsigned F3 five-source complete-call optimum for all 242 nonzero ternary coefficient rows, with one arbitrarily dirty restored connector; exact bill for arbitrary positive source prices and one common readout price.
scope_change_reason: Take the second open question of PR4225: replace its 31 binary-mask demand by full ternary demand in the same unchanged F3 alphabet. This is a local interface side result, not an alphabet extension or supplier admission.
bottleneck_link: Side result. It locates the first demand family where the F3 operator-count floor fails: full ternary demand costs exactly one extra triple of calls. No consumer or recursive saving is established.
stop_rule: Stop after the exhaustive fifteen-event census, two literal 744-call constructions and bounded semantic controls. No larger source count, general price envelope or selected-frontier change.
evidence: verify.py enumerates all 1,401,400 restored fifteen-event paths up to source relabeling (maximum coverage 241 of 242), cross-checks the canonical reduction against full labeled enumeration at two and three sources, shows floor attainment for one to four sources, checks the counting exclusion for seven or more sources, and checks six literal 744-call words by generic coefficients and dense random F3 actions, with five rejection controls and four tariff fixtures.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: What is the exact complete fixed-tariff envelope when readout prices differ?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The common-readout formula needs only lone gaps; arbitrary readout prices need every minimal missing set of a fifteen-event path.
open_questions.first_step: Record the missing sets of every canonical path, close them under source relabeling and keep the inclusion-minimal family.
open_questions.blocked_by: Only the maximum-coverage gaps are recorded here.

open_questions.question: Does full ternary demand on six sources attain the 18 + 3(3^6 - 1) = 2202-call floor?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The floor is attained for n <= 4, fails at n = 5 and is excluded by counting for n >= 7; n = 6 is the only undecided source count.
open_questions.first_step: Port the canonical census to a compiled checker: 190,590,400 canonical eighteen-event paths, or prune with rotation and reversal symmetry.
open_questions.blocked_by: The pure-Python census would exceed the registered replay budget; no consumer for ternary demand is identified.

open_questions.question: Does any concrete caller need full ternary rather than binary demand?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Without a consumer the extra three calls are an interface fact, not a cost change.
open_questions.first_step: Identify an immutable-source, unobserved-output caller whose outputs use coefficient 2.
open_questions.blocked_by: No physical or selected-supplier consumer is instantiated.
